title: Can you draw four pairs of parallel lines?
description: A question from the book asks for four pairs of parallel lines in different orientations. For each line m and a point B off it, a transversal, equal arcs and a copied chord give the line n, and side side side shows each n is parallel to its m.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same transversal-and-copy steps work in any direction, because arcs and chords are only lengths. Watch for students who place E on the wrong side of the transversal when the line is turned.

video_script.why: The child has made one parallel line and now checks that the steps work for lines facing every way.
video_script.substitution: Each pair is made in the same way as the example in the book: a transversal through B, equal arcs at A and B, and the chord carried across, only turned.
video_script.anchor: Construct four pairs of parallel lines in different orientations.
video_script.payoff_line: Each new line n is parallel to its line m

final_answer.value: Four pairs m and n, each made by copying the corresponding angle at A to B (SSS), so each n ∥ m
final_answer.spoken: for each line m, copy the corresponding angle at B, and each new line n is parallel to its line m, by side side side

never_show: the answer card before the reveal
maths_rules: Four lines m run in different directions: across, up and down, and two slanting ways. A point B is marked off each line.
A transversal l through B cuts m at A. An arc with centre A cuts m at C and l at D; the same radius with centre B cuts l at F, beyond B.
The chord CD is carried to F and cuts the arc at E, on the same side of l as C; n is drawn through B and E.
Triangle BFE is congruent to triangle ADC by SSS, so the corresponding angles at B and A are equal and n is parallel to m.
video_script.design: One idea: the same steps work in every direction. The check is the triangle pair, as in the book's example.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Draw an arc that cuts l at F, beyond B.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Draw the line n through B and E. Repeat all this for the other three lines.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the result. Triangles B F E and eigh D C have three pairs of equal sides.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They are congruent by side side side, so the corresponding angles at B and eigh are equal.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel, in every one of the four pairs.
